title: Equal draws from broad sources kept four bumblebee richness-change signs in selected cells in 1901-2014
abstract: We tested whether recorded bumblebee richness changes stayed stable when a sample fixed both total record count and draws from each source. We extended a public climate-impact analysis with exact rarefaction calculations. Four tests used North America and Europe and two disjoint time comparisons within 1901-2014. With ten draws per broad source label, the two sampling designs kept the same mean change sign in all four samples. Source constraints shifted the mean changes upward by 0.05-0.24 expected species per cell. All four adjusted intervals for the paired differences included zero. Finer source labels and other draw sizes gave less stable results. These are selected records, not random field samples. The test measures sensitivity to a sampling design. It does not identify a climate effect, a pollution effect, true richness change or a causal source bias. The package gives code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval instructions. Source records and cell tables remain outside the package.

display.caption: Changes in expected recorded richness in selected one-degree cells. Both designs use the same records and total draw count. One fixes draws by broad source label. Intervals use a geographic block bootstrap with four-test adjustment. Source: Soroye et al. (2020), Figshare version 3; new calculations.
